sectionGaps.title: The Burden of Proof
sectionGaps.suggestion: Proof and logic section. Slot1 can be hand-specified as [1,1,1,0], but general counterexample requests admit many answers and must remain multiple choice or gain a predicate grader.

sectionGaps.title: If and Only If
sectionGaps.suggestion: Biconditionals/classification; all existing answers are concepts, statements, or reasoning. Retain multiple choice or author separate reasoning-oriented numeric examples.

sectionGaps.title: Sides and Angles of a Triangle
sectionGaps.suggestion: Side/angle comparisons answer with labels or inequalities. A single-number grader would alter the learning objective; retain choices.

sectionGaps.title: Pythagoras — Not Just For Right Triangles
sectionGaps.suggestion: Safe numeric count/parameter slots 7-10 are explicitly approved in includeSlots.

sectionGaps.title: Funky Areas
sectionGaps.suggestion: Composite circle areas require pi expressions, not plain rational answers. Keep choices until exact symbolic input is supported; do not silently strip pi.

sectionGaps.title: Translations
sectionGaps.suggestion: Translation questions ask for coordinate pairs or transformation rules; single rational input cannot represent their answer.

sectionGaps.title: Reflections
sectionGaps.suggestion: Other slots require coordinate pairs, symmetry line names, or transformation concepts. One count slot is suitable across all versions.

sectionGaps.title: Chapter challenge
sectionGaps.suggestion: Only one slot is plain numeric across all versions. E.g shortest reflected path slot7 has radicals in three versions; do not force rational input.

sectionGaps.title: Circles
sectionGaps.suggestion: Only radius slot6 is plain numeric in all versions. Slot3 version3 is sqrt(30), so converting the whole slot requires symbolic input.

sectionGaps.title: Proofs with Analytic Geometry
sectionGaps.suggestion: General coordinate proofs deliberately use variables, expressions, and coordinate pairs. Numeric substitutes would weaken the proof objective.

sectionGaps.title: Proofs
sectionGaps.suggestion: Proof justifications/congruence criteria/logical validity are not single numeric answers. Preserve reasoning choices rather than disguising them as numeric entry.

notes: Selected numeric geometry questions retain figure context. Hide choices but retain the figure and mathematical prompt.

Angles and percentages preserve the explicit degree/percent suffix outside the input. Number-only answers in meter/area/volume story problems have units already stated in the prompt; input hint must explicitly say to omit units.

Do not broadly remove all questions containing which: it can be a relative clause in a unique integer-count question. Conversely possible chord/third-side and unbounded counterexample requests depend on the choices and are unsafe.

Do not parse radicals, pi, coordinate pairs, multiple solutions, or expressions as a single rational value. Fraction extraction must match the entire numeric expression; mixed numerals must not concatenate.
